analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: US CPI is the main event today, with headline expected at 0.3% MoM and core at 0.2% MoM. That would be a decent moderation from September, particularly for headline as fuel prices stabilised.

Mizuho sees the asymmetry toward a stronger CPI print. About 80% of a 25bp December Fed hike is priced, and another hike is only priced further into H2-27. A core print of 0.3% or higher would likely pressure the front end and bring 4.90% on the 10Y back into view, with $42bn of 10Y UST supply later today.
USTs struggled against yesterday's sharp equity recovery. 2Y yields reached 4.56%, about 11bp above Friday's pre-NFP lows. The long end held up better as oil fell, leaving the curve flatter.

DXY kept falling despite the more hawkish rates repricing and is moving toward 101.50. Brent extended its move toward $91.5 after Trump signalled further US strikes on Iran are unlikely for now and reports of potential progress on an agreement.
Mizuho would be wary of chasing yesterday's duration move purely on cheaper oil, because no formal deal is confirmed and disruption around Hormuz is not fully resolved.

In EUR rates, 10Y Bund yields briefly fell toward 3.22% before reversing as equities strengthened. BTP-Bund tightened about 3bp and OAT-Bund about 2-3bp, a risk-on relationship Mizuho expects to persist if Iran headlines keep improving.
Mizuho struggles to see a clean Bund rally unless CPI delivers relief, given hawkish US front-end repricing and firm risk sentiment. US CPI matters more for Bund direction than the European calendar.
Mizuho favors EUR steepeners. 2s10s has flattened toward 20bp, German supply is heavier next year, and Mizuho expects the ECB to deliver less tightening than the market's +50bp into H2-27.

10Y Gilt yields fell to 5.08%, the lowest since late August. 30Y yields briefly traded around 5.54%, almost 45bp below the 6% levels tested a month ago. Mizuho is cautious about chasing the move because SONIA prices about a 50% chance of a December BoE hike and two hikes fully priced by April.
Asian equities were risk-on. JGBs bear-steepened after a weak 30Y JGB auction, a mixed BoJ summary of opinions and weak household spending data. USD/JPY stayed in a tight range around 158.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected moderation from September as fuel prices stabilised.
Core is expected to slow more broadly after last month's strength. A 0.3%+ print would likely pressure the front end of the Treasury curve.
Another hike is only priced further into H2-27. Mizuho sees the risk skewed to a stronger CPI print.
Mizuho expects the ECB to deliver less tightening than the market prices.

macro_indicators.reading: ~50% chance of a December hike, two hikes fully priced by April
macro_indicators.interpretation: The front end is sensitive to energy prices and incoming data.

trade_ideas.rationale: 2s10s has flattened toward 20bp, German supply is heavier next year, and the ECB is likely to deliver less tightening than priced.

risk_factors: A core CPI print of 0.3% or higher could pressure the front end and push the 10Y toward 4.90%.
Hormuz disruption and the lack of a formal Iran deal could reverse the oil decline.
Heavy supply today: $42bn 10Y UST, EU 5Y and 20Y syndication of €8-9bn, €3bn of 10Y DSLs and £1bn of 2056 gilts.
Gilt levels already reflect a good deal of good news after the rapid rally.
geopolitical: Trump signalled further US strikes on Iran are unlikely for now, and there are reports of potential progress on an agreement.
No formal Iran deal is confirmed and disruption around Hormuz is not fully resolved.
